checks.finding: Existing queue prevents a second registered invocation. At registration the driver must match its SOURCE_PASS review hash and capacity must record admitted bounded training with zero audit blockers. Actual local capacity audit SHA matches and blockers are zero; the driver rechecks audit hash and reserved23 capacity>=1 at handover.

One remote Python checks tail flags and performs a bounded3s dead-PID exit probe before flushing READY. It then waits original PID1028233 and PID1028232 sequentially with240s intervals; both checked subprocesses must return before the exit message. Tail waits /dev/null without reading training logs, GPU data or sending termination signals. Process exit does not establish training success.

One SSH child receives and closes stdin; READY records actual local waiter, SSH and remote waiter PIDs. Remote program emits only two small JSON lines; tail follows /dev/null, so no recurring stdout stream is left undrained while waiting. Terminal stdout/stderr and SSH return code are recorded, and nonzero SSH or wrong terminal state cannot hand over. A pre-READY failure aborts before queue registration.

Only after successful owner-exit receipt is the reserved23 driver called with check=True. It independently requires old PIDs absent, exact empty compute ownership/<500MiB per reserved card, unique paths and per-plan real M0/native0/reload/frozen/replay before formal startup. RESERVED_FORMALS_STARTED is written only after driver success. There is no retry, fallback, GPU allocation or stop-existing-owner operation in this helper.

runtime_admission: SOURCE_ONLY: waiter and hardware/M0/startup gates not executed by reviewer. GNUtail capability/dead-PID behavior is checked at actual startup before READY.
